## The course

The course is for doctoral students of physics, mathematics, chemistry, biology and geography. Each lecture comes with its slides and with Jupyter notebooks that reproduce every figure and number on the slides. The notebooks run on a laptop CPU or in Google Colab; each page has an *Open in Colab* button.

## Lectures {#lectures}

| | Lecture | Notebooks |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | [Scientific Discovery: from AI to Deep Learning](lectures/lecture-01.qmd) | Labs 001–003: Python, NumPy, PyTorch |
| 2 | [The Recipe of Deep Learning](lectures/lecture-02.qmd) | Labs 004–009: automatic differentiation, universal approximation, training, MNIST |
| 3 | [Convolutional Neural Networks](lectures/lecture-03.qmd) | limits of deep networks: three experiments on blood cells |
| 4 | [CNNs on Scientific Data and the 2D Ising Model](lectures/lecture-04.qmd) | blood cells, convolution and the Ising model, Labs 010–012 |
| 5 | [Unsupervised Learning](lectures/lecture-05.qmd) | PCA, t-SNE, clustering, autoencoders, anomalies |
| 6 | [Generative Models](lectures/lecture-06.qmd) | VAE, conditional generation, GAN, diffusion |

## Main reading

- T. Heightman, M. Płodzień, *Deep Learning in Classical and Quantum Physics*, Springer (to appear, 2027), [arXiv:2508.10666](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.10666)
- A. Dawid, J. Arnold, …, M. Płodzień et al., *Machine Learning in Quantum Sciences*, Cambridge University Press (2025), [arXiv:2204.04198](https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.04198)
